title: What happens inside your body after a bee sting?
sources: Journal of Allergy and Clinical Immunology Melittin

lines.text: When a honeybee stings your skin, what microscopic war explodes inside your bloodstream?
lines.caps: What happens inside your *skin | after a *bee sting?

lines.text: The bee's barbed stinger tears out of its abdomen, continuing to pump venom automatically for minutes.
The venom contains melittin, a powerful peptide that literally punches holes through cell membranes.
Pain receptors fire emergency alarms to your spinal cord while mast cells release waves of histamine.
lines.caps: Mast cells flood tissue with *waves | of burning *histamine

lines.text: Blood vessels dilate to rush white blood cells to the scene, causing rapid swelling and fiery redness.
lines.caps: Capillaries dilate to rush *immune cells | causing *swelling

lines.text: White blood cells gobble up venom fragments over three days until the swelling recedes.
lines.caps: White blood cells *clean up | the venom over *3 days

lines.text: Scrape the stinger off immediately with a credit card to stop the venom pump early.
lines.caps: Scrape the stinger *off fast | to stop the *venom pump!
